notes.claim: A flywheel with a higher moment of inertia, meaning more mass or mass further from the centre, stores more energy at the same speed.
Rotational power is torque times angular velocity, with the speed in radians per second.
A flywheel evens out the speed variations an engine's fluctuating torque would cause, as on a diesel generator (added for i6 at review).

sources.title: Motor Calculations.PDF — Michigan Technological University
sources.quote: In calculating rotational power, it is necessary to convert the velocity to units of rad/sec.

sources.title: How do flywheels store energy? - Explain that Stuff — Explain that Stuff
sources.quote: a flywheel will store more energy if it has either a higher moment of inertia (more mass or mass positioned further from its center)
